content: 1. When ozanimod is co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, close monitoring is required. Both ozanimod and lopinavir can prolong the QTc interval, necessitating therapy modification or close monitoring. Initiating ozanimod in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties is generally not recommended. 2. Lopinavir increases paclitaxel levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered to avoid serious interactions. Similarly, lopinavir increases the levels of protein-bound paclitaxel via the same mechanism, requiring avoidance or substitution with an alternative drug. 3. Lopinavir significantly increases pacritinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of severe toxicity. 4. Lopinavir increases palbociclib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 5. Lopinavir increases palovarotene levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. 6. Lopinavir increases panobinostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is required. Both lopinavir and panobinostat prolong the QTc interval, and their combination is not recommended due to the risk of significant QT prolongation. 7. Lopinavir increases paricalcitol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity. 8. Lopinavir and pasireotide both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification or close monitoring is necessary to mitigate the risk of arrhythmias. 9. Lopinavir increases pazopanib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. 10. Pentobarbital decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Lopinavir increases pexidartinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pexidartinib dose may be resumed. 12. Phenobarbital decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Phenytoin decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Lopinavir increases pimavanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. Both lopinavir and pimavanserin prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. 15. Lopinavir increases pimozide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of severe toxicity. 16. Lopinavir increases pirtobrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib during the use of strong CYP3A inhibitors. Once the inhibitor is discontinued for five half-lives, resume the previous pirtobrutinib dose. 17. Lopinavir increases pitavastatin levels by inhibiting metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of severe toxicity. 18. Lopinavir and pitolisant both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. 19. Lopinavir increases polatuzumab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, and monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), which is a CYP3A4 substrate. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase MMAE exposure, leading to increased toxicity. 20. Lopinavir increases pomalidomide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. 21. Lopinavir increases ponatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the ponatinib starting dose to 30 mg daily. 22. Posaconazole increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Lopinavir increases pralsetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. 24. Lopinavir decreases pramlintide effects due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Lopinavir increases praziquantel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Prednisone decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Lopinavir and primaquine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. 28. Primidone decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Lopinavir increases quazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. 30. Lopinavir and quetiapine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. Lopinavir increases quetiapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. 31. Lopinavir increases quinidine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. 32. Lopinavir and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. Lopinavir increases quinine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. 33. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Lopinavir increases quizartinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. If co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the quizartinib dose to 4 mg/day. Interrupt quizartinib during the use of strong CYP3A inhibitors. 35. Lopinavir increases ranolazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of severe toxicity. 36. Lopinavir increases red yeast rice levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. Red yeast rice contains monacolin K, which is chemically identical to lovastatin, and may increase the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. 37. Lopinavir increases regorafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of severe toxicity. 38. Lopinavir increases repaglinide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Lopinavir increases repotrectinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. 40. Lopinavir increases resmetirom levels by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transporters. Avoid co-administration with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors. 41. Ribociclib increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. Both ribociclib and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. 42. Rifabutin decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. 43. Rifampin decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. 44. Rifapentine decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Lopinavir increases rifaximin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Lopinavir increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine increases lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. 47. Lopinavir increases rimegepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. 48. Lopinavir increases riociguat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. Monitor for signs of hypotension and reduce the dose if necessary. 49. Ritonavir increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Lopinavir increases rivaroxaban levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use with combined P-glycoprotein and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors due to the risk of increased bleeding. 51. Lopinavir decreases roflumilast levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 52. Lopinavir increases roflumilast topical levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Lopinavir increases romidepsin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. 54. Lopinavir decreases rosiglitazone effects due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Lopinavir increases rosuvastatin levels by inhibiting metabolism. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. Limit rosuvastatin dose to 10 mg/day. 56. Rucaparib increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 57. Rufinamide decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Lopinavir increases ruxolitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. Reduce the ruxolitinib starting dose to 10 mg BID with platelet counts ≥100 x 10^9/L. Avoid use with platelet counts <100 x 10^9/L. 59. Lopinavir increases salmeterol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of severe toxicity. 60. Lopinavir increases saxagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely.
